title: Italian Game: develop, castle, break
objective: Bring out your pieces, keep your king safe, then push the d-pawn.

commentary_source.name: Uroschess original synthetic lesson
commentary_source.attribution: Original instructional text and synthetic Italian Game line

steps.explanation: Both sides have a pawn in the centre and a knight developed. White can bring out the king bishop next.
steps.detail: Bc4 creates the Italian Game. The bishop becomes active and White gets closer to castling.

question.prompt: Develop the bishop to an active square.
hints: Look at the bishop on f1.

answers.feedback: Bc4 enters the Italian Game, develops actively, and prepares castling.
Bb5 is excellent too. It enters the Spanish Game and still develops with purpose.
Be2 is quieter, but it develops and clears the castling path.
Ng1 moves a developed piece backward. Bring a new piece into the game instead.

question.other_legal_move_text: That move may be playable, but this exercise asks for useful bishop development.

steps.explanation: White has brought out pieces and made the king safe. The pawn on c3 helps the d-pawn move forward.
steps.detail: Push the d-pawn to d4 to attack Black's e5 pawn. If Black takes it, White can take back.

question.prompt: Play the d4 break, then recapture in the centre.
hints: Push the pawn from d3 to d4.
After ...exd4, use the c-pawn or knight to recapture.

children.feedback: Black exchanges in the centre. Recapture the pawn.
cxd4 restores White's central pawn and opens the c-file.
Nxd4 also recaptures and places the knight in the centre.

question.other_legal_move_text: That move leaves the planned d4 break. Explore it, then return to practise the central break.

takeaway: In the Italian Game, develop and castle first; then prepare d4 to challenge the centre.
